sections.content:
21,920 people

were counted on the census as "road construction operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Road construction operatives construct, repair and maintain roads and lay paving slabs and kerbstones to form pavements and street gutters.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "road construction operatives" there were more men than women (97.9% compared with 2.1%).

This means "road construction operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 97.9% and women made up 2.1% of "road construction operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "road construction operatives" included:

  • welding trades
  • vehicle body builders and repairers
  • stonemasons and related trades

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "road construction operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "road construction operatives", 13.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "road construction operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "road construction operatives" included:

  • catering and bar managers
  • rail construction and maintenance operatives
  • aerospace engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "road construction operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "road construction operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "road construction operatives", 7.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.8% compared with 6.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (70.2%) than self-employed (29.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Dudley, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
